stages.name: Beyond Rome
stages.desc: Independent peoples and kingdoms outside Roman rule

stages.name: Client kingdoms
stages.desc: Allied kings: Numidia, Mauretania, Ptolemaic Egypt

stages.name: Pompeian-held
stages.desc: Held by Pompey, his sons or Caesar's assassins

stages.name: Caesarian-held
stages.desc: Held by Caesar or his heirs, the triumvirs

stages.name: Garamantes campaign
stages.desc: Balbus the Younger's desert war, 20–19 BC

states.name: France
timeline: Free Gaul; Rome holds only the southern strip, Transalpine Gaul, and Massilia is its ally
Caesar's command: the conquest of Gaul begins
Vercingetorix surrenders at Alesia
Massilia, siding with Pompey, is besieged and taken
Antony and Lepidus hold Gaul for the Caesarians
Augustus organises the Gallic provinces

states.name: Morocco
timeline: The kingdom of Mauretania, Rome's ally since the war against Jugurtha
Kings Bogud and Bocchus side with Caesar
Balbus the Younger flees to King Bogud with Gades' treasure
Bocchus seizes Bogud's kingdom while Bogud fights for Antony in Spain
Bocchus dies; Mauretania is ruled by Octavian's officers
Mauretania is administered directly by Rome
Augustus makes Juba II, son of Juba I, king of Mauretania

states.name: Albania
timeline: The Adriatic coast of Macedonia: Dyrrachium and Apollonia
Pompey's base at Dyrrachium
After Pharsalus the coast passes to Caesar
Brutus holds the Adriatic coast
Philippi: the coast returns to the triumvirs
Part of the province of Macedonia

states.name: Turkey
timeline: Pontus, Bithynia, Cappadocia and Galatia are independent; Rome holds only the province of Asia
Mithridates of Pontus overruns Asia and orders the killing of Romans and Italians
Pompey's settlement: new provinces and allied kings across Anatolia
The East raises ships, money and troops for Pompey
After Pharsalus the East goes over to Caesar
Caesar defeats Pharnaces at Zela: 'I came, I saw, I conquered'
Cassius squeezes the cities of Asia for money for the Republican armies
After Philippi Antony governs the East
Augustus' provinces and client kings

states.name: Spain
timeline: Hither and Further Spain are Roman provinces; Gades, a Tyrian colony, is Rome's ally by treaty; the far north is unconquered
Sertorius, a Roman rebel, raises the Iberians and Lusitanians against Sulla's regime
Gades' treaty of alliance with Rome is renewed
Sertorius is murdered; Pompey makes Balbus and his family Roman citizens
Caesar, quaestor in Further Spain, visits the temple of Hercules-Melqart at Gades
Caesar governs Further Spain, with Balbus as his chief of engineers
Spain becomes Pompey's province, governed through his legates Afranius and Petreius
Caesar wins at Ilerda; Gades receives Roman citizenship
Pompey's sons raise Further Spain against Caesar
Caesar wins at Munda, his last battle
Balbus the Younger, quaestor at Gades, rules it like a king, then flees to Mauretania
Augustus divides Spain into provinces; war goes on in the Cantabrian north
Agrippa ends the Cantabrian Wars; all of Spain is Roman

states.name: Libya
timeline: The Garamantes rule the Fezzan; Cyrene is still a Ptolemaic kingdom
Ptolemy Apion leaves Cyrenaica to Rome in his will
Cyrenaica becomes a Roman province; the desert interior stays Garamantian
Cyrenaica is held for Pompey
Cato marches the Pompeian survivors west across the Syrtes
After Thapsus the coast submits to Caesar; Lepcis is fined
Antony gives Cyrenaica to his daughter by Cleopatra
The province of Crete and Cyrenaica
Balbus the Younger marches from Sabratha into the Sahara, taking Cydamus and Garama
The Garamantes are humbled; Balbus triumphs in Rome on 27 March

states.name: Tunisia
timeline: The province of Africa, on the land of ruined Carthage, Tyre's greatest colony
Africa is held for Pompey; Curio's invasion fails
Caesar wins at Thapsus; Cato kills himself at Utica
Caesar orders a new Roman colony at Carthage
Lepidus holds Africa as his share of the triumvirate
The province of Africa Proconsularis
Balbus the Younger becomes proconsul of Africa

states.name: Greece
timeline: The provinces of Macedonia and Achaea
Mithridates' armies overrun Greece; Sulla retakes Athens in 86
Pompey gathers the Senate's armies in Macedonia and Greece
Caesar defeats Pompey at Pharsalus
Brutus seizes Macedonia and Greece for the Republican cause
Antony and Octavian defeat Brutus and Cassius at Philippi
Octavian defeats Antony and Cleopatra at Actium
Achaea becomes a separate province

states.name: Italy
timeline: Rome and its Italian allies
The Social War: Rome's Italian allies revolt and win citizenship
Sulla wins the civil war and rules as dictator
Balbus arrives in Rome with Pompey
Balbus' citizenship is challenged in court; Cicero wins the case
Caesar crosses the Rubicon; Pompey abandons Italy
Caesar is murdered; Balbus joins his young heir Octavian
Balbus is consul, the first foreign-born man to hold the office
Octavian becomes Augustus
Balbus the Younger celebrates his triumph in Rome

states.name: Algeria
timeline: The kingdom of Numidia, Rome's client after Jugurtha's defeat
King Juba I of Numidia destroys Curio's Caesarian army in Africa
After Thapsus Juba dies; Caesar annexes Numidia as Africa Nova, governed by Sallust
The province of Africa
Juba II rules western Algeria from his capital Caesarea; the east stays Roman

states.name: Portugal
timeline: Lusitanians and Callaeci: Rome holds only the south, and raids and revolts are frequent
The Lusitanians invite Sertorius to lead them against Rome's governors
Caesar campaigns to the Atlantic and the far north-west; Lusitania is pacified
Part of Pompey's Spanish command
Pompey's legates surrender; Caesar's governors take over
Lusitania rises for Pompey's sons
After Munda the south-west returns to Caesar
The new province of Lusitania is created

states.name: Egypt
timeline: The Ptolemaic kingdom, rich and dependent on Rome's favour
Caesar and Pompey have Ptolemy XII recognised as 'friend and ally' for six thousand talents
Pompey is murdered at Pelusium; Caesar is besieged in Alexandria
Caesar places Cleopatra on the throne
Antony and Cleopatra's Donations of Alexandria
Antony and Cleopatra die; Egypt becomes a Roman province

events.title: Balbus is born
events.text: Lucius Cornelius Balbus is born, about this time, into a leading Punic family of Gades.

events.title: Temple of Melqart
events.text: Gades' great temple of Melqart, the Tyrian god the Romans call Hercules, draws pilgrims and merchants.

events.title: Social War
events.text: Rome's Italian allies revolt; they win Roman citizenship, a precedent Balbus' case will lean on.

events.title: Mithridates' massacre
events.text: Mithridates of Pontus has tens of thousands of Romans and Italians killed in Asia.

events.title: Sulla's dictatorship
events.text: Sulla wins the civil war and rules Rome by proscription.

events.title: Sertorius in Spain
events.text: The Roman rebel Sertorius lands in Spain and leads Lusitanians and Iberians against Sulla's generals.

events.title: Treaty of Gades
events.text: Rome renews its treaty of alliance with Gades, first made in 206 BC.

events.title: Pompey to Spain
events.text: Young Pompey is sent to Spain; Balbus serves under him and Metellus Pius.

events.title: Cyrenaica annexed
events.text: Rome makes Cyrenaica a province, twenty-two years after its king left it to Rome.

events.title: Balbus made Roman
events.text: Under the law of the consuls Gellius and Lentulus, Pompey grants citizenship to Balbus and his family.

events.title: To Rome
events.text: Balbus follows Pompey to Rome, where his wealth and tact open every door.

events.title: Caesar at Gades
events.text: Caesar, a quaestor, sees Alexander's statue in the temple at Gades and weeps at his own lack of achievement.

events.title: Pompey in the East
events.text: Pompey reorganises Anatolia and the Levant after defeating Mithridates.

events.title: Caesar's engineer
events.text: Caesar governs Further Spain; Balbus is his praefectus fabrum, chief of engineers.

events.title: The go-between
events.text: Balbus carries Caesar's offer to Cicero to join the alliance with Pompey and Crassus.

events.title: Gallic War
events.text: Caesar begins eight years of conquest in Gaul; Balbus manages his affairs and money.

events.title: Pro Balbo
events.text: Balbus is prosecuted for usurping citizenship; Pompey, Crassus and Cicero defend him, and he is acquitted.

events.title: Alesia
events.text: Vercingetorix surrenders to Caesar after the siege of Alesia.

events.title: The Rubicon
events.text: Caesar crosses the Rubicon in January; Balbus stays in Rome to work for him.

events.title: Gades enfranchised
events.text: Caesar gives every free man of Gades Roman citizenship.

events.title: Ilerda
events.text: Caesar forces Pompey's legates in Spain to surrender at Ilerda.

events.title: Curio's defeat
events.text: King Juba of Numidia destroys Caesar's army in Africa on the Bagradas.

events.title: Dyrrachium
events.text: Pompey breaks out of Caesar's siege lines on the Adriatic coast.

events.title: Pharsalus
events.text: Caesar crushes Pompey's army in Thessaly on 9 August.

events.title: Pompey murdered
events.text: Pompey is stabbed to death as he lands in Egypt.

events.title: Zela
events.text: Caesar defeats Pharnaces of Pontus: 'I came, I saw, I conquered.'

events.title: Thapsus
events.text: Caesar defeats the Pompeians and King Juba; Numidia becomes a province.

events.title: Munda
events.text: Caesar defeats Pompey's sons in southern Spain, his last battle.

events.title: Ides of March
events.text: Caesar is murdered; Balbus attaches himself to the young Octavian.

events.title: Terror at Gades
events.text: Balbus the Younger, quaestor, burns a Pompeian veteran alive at Gades, then flees to King Bogud.

events.title: Philippi
events.text: Antony and Octavian defeat Brutus and Cassius in Macedonia.

events.title: Consul Balbus
events.text: Balbus becomes consul, the first man born outside Italy to hold Rome's highest office.

events.title: Bogud dethroned
events.text: Bocchus takes western Mauretania while its king fights for Antony.

events.title: Actium
events.text: Octavian's fleet defeats Antony and Cleopatra off western Greece.

events.title: Egypt annexed
events.text: Antony and Cleopatra die at Alexandria; Egypt becomes Roman.

events.title: Augustus
events.text: Octavian takes the name Augustus and divides the provinces with the Senate.

events.title: Juba II
events.text: Juba II, raised in Rome, becomes king of Mauretania with his capital at Caesarea.

events.title: New Gades
events.text: Balbus the Younger builds Gades a new town and a mainland harbour.

events.title: Into the Sahara
events.text: Balbus the Younger marches from Sabratha and takes Cydamus, today's Ghadames.

events.title: Garama falls
events.text: Balbus takes Garama, capital of the Garamantes, deep in the Fezzan.

events.title: Triumph
events.text: On 27 March Balbus the Younger triumphs in Rome, the only foreign-born man ever to do so.

eras: A Tyrian City in Rome's West
chartNote: Share of the mapped area of today's countries, Portugal to Egypt, by the power that held most of each country. A simplification: ancient borders ran through modern ones, and loyalties shifted within a year. The view is clipped at about 24°N and 37°E, and the desert countries of North Africa weigh heavily in the shares.
